claim_verdicts.evidence: Definitional: this is the name-giving formulation of the principle. Local .NET docs use the same idea without the exact wording: "it helps you to follow the open/closed principle in the sending service. That way, additional subscribers can be added in the future without the need to modify the sender service." No page in refs/dotnet-docs contains "open for extension ... closed for modification" verbatim (grep).

git show stage-0: Smells.cs lines 8-9 `ShippingVnd(int totalVnd, bool express, bool loyal, bool pickUp, string city, int weightGram)` (six params); line 11 `if (!pickUp)` first; returns on lines 18, 19, 22, 23, 26 all use `express ? ... : ...`; line 29 `return 0;`. Six returns, five read express. Code block lines 8-30 matches source character-for-character.

git show stage-0: line 5 `public abstract class ShippingFee`, line 7 `public abstract int ForOrder(int totalVnd);`, lines 10/15/20 `public sealed class` StandardShipping/ExpressShipping/PickUpInStore, line 12 `totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000`, line 17 `60_000`, line 22 `0`. Code block lines 5-23 matches source character-for-character.

"A non-abstract class derived from an abstract class must include actual implementations of all inherited abstract methods and accessors." (abstract.md:47). CS0534: "'function1' does not implement inherited abstract member 'function2' ... A class is required to implement all the abstract members in the base class, unless the class is also abstract." Tried to confirm with dotnet build in a scratch copy; command was not permitted, so evidence is docs only.

git show stage-0:samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests/SamplesTests.cs lines 7-25: class ShippingFeeTests; StandardShippingIsFreeFromTwoMillion asserts 30_000 at 1_999_999 and 0 at 2_000_000; EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall builds the three kinds explicitly and asserts {0, 60_000, 0} at 2_000_000. Neither test enumerates subclasses, so a new subclass leaves both unchanged (by inspection; test run not permitted).

"An abstract method is implicitly a virtual method." (abstract.md:53). "When you invoke a virtual method, the runtime checks the type of the object for an overriding member. It calls the overriding member in the most derived class." (virtual.md:28). A ShippingFee caller of ForOrder needs no edit. Creation part is hedged ("possibly"/"may"): at stage-0 only SamplesTests.cs:12,21 creates kinds; no creation site exists to contradict it.

Follows from the definition in claim 1: OCP constrains how a new case is added; editing StandardShipping's own threshold (ShippingFee.cs:12) is changing an existing rule, not adding a case. Stated in the lesson with its condition ("because the rule itself changed").

Tautological given the stated condition: if a caller branches on the concrete class, a new class requires editing that branch. The lesson states it conditionally ("If callers checked which class they had..."), not as an absolute.

git show stage-0: Smells.cs:6 `public static class Smells`, ShippingVnd is a static method taking the kind as bool flags (line 9); a static class "Is sealed" (static-classes...md:46), so no subclass/override can add a kind: a new flag must be read inside the method body, before or among the six returns (lines 18,19,22,23,26,29). Re-checking neighbouring returns is the stated consequence, not a documented rule.

git show stage-0: Smells.cs:9 params include `string city, int weightGram`; lines 13,15 branch on them; line 26 returns 90000/45000 outside Hà Nội/Hồ Chí Minh. ShippingFee.cs:7 `ForOrder(int totalVnd)` only; StandardShipping returns 30_000 below 2_000_000 regardless of city. So e.g. standard, other city, 1,000,000 VND: 45000 vs 30_000 — different rules.

issues.text: Summary line 3 says the kind of shipping is spread across the five `express` lines only; section 5 correctly says it is also `pickUp`, checked at the top. The summary drops half of how the kind is encoded.
issues.quote: `Smells.ShippingVnd` spreads the kind of shipping across five `express` lines, so a new kind means editing that method and re-checking them.
issues.fix: "`Smells.ShippingVnd` spreads the kind of shipping across a `pickUp` check and five `express` returns, so a new kind means editing that method and re-checking them."

issues.text: After being told OCP means not editing existing code, I read that some code still has to create the new kind. I cannot tell whether that creating code already exists (and so gets edited) or is new, nor why editing it would be fine under OCP. 'Sits outside the fee rules' reads like an escape hatch without the reason.
issues.quote: Some code still has to create the new kind, but that code sits outside the fee rules; the rules that already work are not edited.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one saying plainly: that creating code may need a small edit, and OCP here is about keeping the fee rules and their callers closed, not every line in the program.

issues.text: The situation says both places 'work out a shipping fee', so I expected the same rules. Comparing the code blocks, `Smells.ShippingVnd` depends on city and weight (45000/90000 outside two cities) while `StandardShipping`/`ExpressShipping` ignore city. I stopped to wonder whether the class version is a rewrite of the flag version or a different, simpler rule set.
issues.quote: The samples project already works out a shipping fee in two places
issues.fix: Add half a sentence in section 2 or 5 saying the two versions do not compute exactly the same rules; they are compared only for where a new kind would go.

issues.text: q2 explanation for option d mentions 'modules', a word the lesson never uses; it made me wonder if OCP covers something beyond classes that I missed.
issues.quote: OCP is usually applied to classes and modules — in the lesson, to the shipping classes.
issues.fix: Replace with: "OCP is not limited to methods; in the lesson it is applied to the shipping classes."
